## Datacenter Power Systems: Free Interactive Course | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/

Datacenter Twin Lab

Learn datacenter continuity and Infrastructure Engineering with 24 free, interactive
browser lessons.

A generator fails. How long does the battery last?

In the canonical 1 MW example, a 100 kWh battery delivers 85.5 kWh after discharge and
distribution losses. That supplies the load for 307.8 seconds after utility and generator
fail at 300 seconds, with depletion at 607.8 seconds elapsed. Charging is disabled.
Predict the result, run the experiment, then explain the energy balance.

The interactive interface starts automatically when its scripts load. The hosted demo uses
JavaScript. Optional Python verification downloads its runtime only when you request it.
Calculations run on your device; no account is required.

JavaScript is disabled. Use the Python quickstart or read the worked
example below.

## About, Model Scope & Reproducibility | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/about/

About the lab / evidence you can inspect
Understand the model. Reproduce the result.

Datacenter Twin Lab is a local-first power-continuity what-if simulator and a 24-lesson course for datacenter engineers.

Created and maintained by Mohammad Rezwan Khan. Visit the engineering profile and publications. The project is open source under Apache-2.0. It runs on your device without an account or shared simulation backend.

Development and educational writing use AI assistance. Numerical examples are checked with stated equations, the Python reference engine and browser tests; those maintainer checks are distinct from independent external review. Inspect the reference results and complete records to follow a claim back to its inputs.

How long does 100 kWh support a 1 MW load?
For this fixed-load example, 100 kWh × 0.90 discharge efficiency × 0.95 distribution efficiency = 85.5 kWh delivered. That is 307.8 seconds at 1,000 kW. With 50 kWh, it is 153.9 seconds. Charging is disabled; utility and generator fail at 300 seconds and recover at 900 seconds.
Read the assumptions and run the experiment →

What the simulator does
It accounts for finite battery energy, charging and losses, generator startup and failure, surviving-path capacity, shared failure domains, timed recovery and unserved energy. The fast JavaScript path can be checked on demand against the Python reference. Eighteen presets and twelve continuity lessons use explicit inputs and unit-labelled results. Twelve Infrastructure Engineering lessons add separate bounded educational screens, with their assumptions and engineering HOLD visible.

What the evidence means
The tests and published packets establish reproducible software behavior for the declared inputs. They do not establish facility calibration, AC transients, protection coordination, GPU workload performance, grid adequacy, certified uptime or equipment safety. This software does not control equipment. Independent external reproduction has not yet been obtained.

Inspect or cite the work
Version 2.0.1 source
Published releases and packages
Canonical input equations and reconstruction instructions
Versioned evidence manifest with per-file hashes
Author and software citation record
External reproduction protocol and scope
Install and run with Python

How to contribute
Try one lesson, note anything confusing and describe the steps to reproduce it. A clearer explanation, a documentation fix or an independently derived example can help the next learner. Read the contribution guide or open an issue.

## Datacenter Power Continuity: Results & Reproducibility Evidence

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/evidence/

Reference desk / inputs, arithmetic, evidence

Check the number.
Cite the evidence.

Three datacenter power-continuity cases you can calculate by hand, run in the browser and reproduce in Python.

Original examples by Mohammad Rezwan Khan · Engine 2.0.1 · Citation and source revision

Battery runtime answerThree reference casesReproduce the resultsCite the work

How long does 100 kWh supply a 1 MW load?

307.8 seconds in this charging-disabled example. Stored energy × discharge efficiency × distribution efficiency gives delivered energy: 100 × 0.90 × 0.95 = 85.5 kWh. Divide by 1,000 kW and multiply by 3,600 to convert hours to seconds. With 50 kWh, the same assumptions give 153.9 seconds.

These are durations after the utility outage. With the outage beginning at 300 s, depletion occurs at 607.8 s or 453.9 s elapsed. An event timestamp and a ride-through duration describe different quantities.

Run the 100 / 50 kWh lesson →

Original calculation diagram. Duration starts at the utility outage; it is not an elapsed event timestamp.

Three reference cases, one inspectable ledger

The battery cases use 1,000 kW IT demand, 100 or 50 kWh opening energy, charging disabled, utility and generator failure at 300 s and recovery at 900 s, 90% discharge efficiency and 95% distribution efficiency. For path maintenance, one 700 kW gross path remains for 600 s: it delivers 665 kW and leaves a 335 kW deficit.

307.8 seconds of battery ride-through

The energy table rounds to six decimal places; the case summaries may be shorter. JSON records retain the complete decimal strings and interval ledger. Input-hash filenames identify each configuration; retain the source revision and manifest when citing a result.

Reproduce the result before using it

Download the version 2.0.1 source archive, or check out the exact public source revision linked below. Separately published packages are listed under published releases.

From that source directory, build and verify the three-case packet with Python 3.12 or later:

python scripts/build_evidence.py --output outputs/reproduction-2.0.1
python scripts/build_evidence.py --verify outputs/reproduction-2.0.1

Reconstruct the ledger from its terms, independently of the reported residual: source energy equals served IT energy plus the change in stored battery energy and the conversion losses. Requested IT energy equals served plus unserved IT energy.

Equations, exact configuration and ledger reconstruction

Reproduction method and decimal tolerance

Packet builder and verifier at the cited source

Versioned expected-versus-observed receipt

Cite the claim and its configuration

Mohammad Rezwan Khan. Datacenter Twin Lab, version 2.0.1. Synthetic continuity reference cases. https://khanlab.co.technology/evidence/

For numerical reuse, include the case name, input SHA-256, engine version, result file and exact source revision. Documentation for this build: f2e9cd40a84e6f34bb5c714b5e4361b32bc096ce. Use the software citation record for author and repository details.

This is a software reproduction record, not a peer-reviewed paper or a calibrated facility dataset. No DOI or independent external reproduction is asserted. Original code and inputs are Apache-2.0; source notices describe the material included.

What can these results support?
They support learning about finite reserve, losses, outage timing and path capacity for the stated synthetic inputs. They do not establish equipment suitability, facility uptime, grid adequacy, GPU job performance or physical safety. See the model scope and authorship and external reproduction protocol.

## Interrupt a 50 MW AI cluster | Datacenter Power Lesson 10

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/ai-outage/

Lesson 10 / 12 · Aggregate AI power demand

Interrupt a 50 MW AI cluster
How long can 5 MWh of stored energy bridge a 50 MW load?

By Mohammad Rezwan Khan · Engine 2.0.1 · Cite this lesson

Run this browser lesson →

Predict before you run
Write down your prediction, then change only the input below. In the interactive lesson, compare the starting case with the challenge and export a worksheet to retain your reasoning.

The two lesson configurations
InputStarting valueChallenge value
Initial battery5000 kWh2500 kWh

Reported quantity: s elapsed. The live control accepts 0–5000 kWh.

Worked answer Link to this answer
Scaling the electrical ratings and storage by 50 preserves the 307.8 s ride-through duration. Halving initial reserve gives depletion at 478.2675 s with pre-outage charging. This is aggregate demand, not GPU job or grid adequacy simulation.

Challenge2500 kWh478.2675

## Bridge generator startup | Datacenter Power Lesson 4

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/generator-delay/

Lesson 04 / 12 · Sequence and delay

Bridge generator startup
What changes when startup takes 60 seconds instead of 30?

By Mohammad Rezwan Khan · Engine 2.0.1 · Cite this lesson

Run this browser lesson →

Predict before you run
Write down your prediction, then change only the input below. In the interactive lesson, compare the starting case with the challenge and export a worksheet to retain your reasoning.

The two lesson configurations
InputStarting valueChallenge value
Generator start delay30 s60 s

Reported quantity: s elapsed. The live control accepts 0–600 s.

Worked answer Link to this answer
A utility failure at 300 s requests a start. A 30 s delay makes the generator ready at 330 s; a 60 s delay makes it ready at 360 s. The battery bridges both in these inputs.

Starting case30 s330
Challenge60 s360

## Add a failed generator | Datacenter Power Lesson 5

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/generator-failure/

Add a failed generator
What changes if the generator cannot start?

By Mohammad Rezwan Khan · Engine 2.0.1 · Cite this lesson

Run this browser lesson →

Predict before you run
Write down your prediction, then change only the input below. In the interactive lesson, compare the starting case with the challenge and export a worksheet to retain your reasoning.

The two lesson configurations
InputStarting valueChallenge value
Generator available (0 = failed, 1 = available)0 1 

Reported quantity: s unserved. The live control accepts 0–1.

Worked answer Link to this answer
With the generator failed, the battery empties at 607.8 s and service is lost for 292.2 s. An available generator starts after 30 s and avoids that gap.

## Power Systems for Datacenter Engineers | Free Course Notes

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/

A generator fails. The battery takes over. Can you predict when the lights go out?

## 23. Build an integrated commissioning evidence loop | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/commissioning-evidence-loop/

A completed component test answers a component question. Integrated continuity requires an initial state, expected sequence, instruments, acceptance criteria, stop conditions and recovery boundary that span the service chain. Compare two clocks, then examine the measurement boundary behind an apparently precise efficiency number.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 13. Build an evidence-controlled load ledger | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/evidence-load-ledger/

Begin where the original course leaves off: not with a bigger battery, but with a more disciplined definition of demand. A facility total is meaningful only when every term belongs to the same boundary and operating condition. In this lesson, a 20 MW IT allocation becomes a traceable facility ledger, while a second example demonstrates why conflicting source values must remain visible.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 22. Review spatial capacity and phased development | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/facilities-phased-development/

A rack count is not a facility plan. Equipment requires service space, replacement routes, structural capacity and coordinated boundaries through every construction phase. Use the manuscript’s historical operating account to practise reporting what was actually stated without turning different area descriptions into one misleading density metric.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 16. Audit generator banks and usable fuel | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/generator-bank-fuel/

The original startup lessons ask whether a generator becomes available in time. This lesson asks a different question: can the available bank carry the backed load at all? Follow a source claim through its real-power conversion, post-loss capacity and fuel ledger. A failed arithmetic claim should stay failed even when the combined installed nameplates look impressive.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 19. Inspect grounding, distortion and control-power loops | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/grounding-power-quality/

Low resistance, low distortion and a nominal battery voltage each answer only a narrowly defined question. This lesson turns those single numbers into explicit boundaries. Follow the ground current, compare harmonic denominators, and include the return conductor in the trip circuit before drawing any conclusion about service.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 24. Audit the correction before releasing the design | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/integrated-design-release/

The final lesson asks for a justified release decision, not the largest possible green score. Bring capacity, connectivity, protection, thermal behaviour, controls and evidence together. Then audit a proposed correction from the manuscript’s separate campus example: a remedy is another engineering assertion and must be recalculated.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 21. Separate physical routes, optical budgets and fabric capacity | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/network-optical-budget/

Two fibres are not automatically two independent services, and a low optical loss is not automatically an application pass. Separate the physical administration route from the logical fabric, then calculate a narrow loss budget and post-uplink-loss capacity. The lesson adds communications reasoning without pretending that the existing electrical simulator already models packets.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 18. Trace protection zones and the full trip chain | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/protection-trip-chain/

Protection is not a green status field at one current. It is a chain from the actual fault through measurement, logic, DC supply and interruption. Use a declared inverse-time curve to learn how a calculation behaves, then inspect what that curve cannot establish about CT saturation, electrical zones or selectivity.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 14. Test capacity, paths and common dependencies | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/resilience-state-matrix/

The existing lessons show how a surviving path or shared controller can govern electrical service. Now extend that intuition into a state matrix. Installed equipment, connected equipment and independently substitutable equipment are different sets. A spare counts only when it can reach the required load in the state being assessed.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 20. Coordinate liquid cooling and thermal ride-through | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/thermal-liquid-continuity/

Battery minutes do not create cooling minutes. Start with the manuscript’s mixed-cooling rack, then move to a separately labelled facility thermal model. The visual goal is to make both heat paths and their shared rejection boundary visible, so that the learner never mistakes a liquid-cooled label for complete removal of room heat.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 15. Declare transformer and fault-current boundaries | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/transformer-fault-boundaries/

A current value without its voltage, power base and network boundary is easy to misuse. This lesson builds a small equivalent circuit in layers, then shows how changing an assumption changes a fault-current screen. The purpose is to expose model limits before equipment selection, not to turn an attractive fault animation into a completed short-circuit study.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

## 17. Separate UPS power, battery energy and trip DC | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/infrastructure/ups-battery-station-dc/

The battery lesson already distinguishes reserve from ride-through. Now separate three further boundaries: AC output energy, delivered DC energy and nominal end-of-life storage. Then examine the protection DC circuit, where enough ampere-hours can coexist with insufficient voltage at the device that must operate.
Engineering HOLD
These are bounded educational screens, not an approved design or certification. Educational publication was approved by the owner on 12 October 2026; that decision does not clear engineering evidence.

Are two paths enough when either one must carry the whole load?

Worked answer Link to this answer
One 700 kW path delivers 665 kW after losses, leaving 335 kW unmet. One 1,100 kW path can deliver the full 1,000 kW request. This tests a capacity condition, not a complete N+1 classification.

## Power becomes energy | Datacenter Power Lesson 1

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/power-energy/

Lesson 01 / 12 · kW and kWh

Power becomes energy
How much energy does a constant load request in half an hour?

By Mohammad Rezwan Khan · Engine 2.0.1 · Cite this lesson

Run this browser lesson →

Predict before you run
Write down your prediction, then change only the input below. In the interactive lesson, compare the starting case with the challenge and export a worksheet to retain your reasoning.

The two lesson configurations
InputStarting valueChallenge value
IT demand1000 kW500 kW

Reported quantity: kWh. The live control accepts 0–1000 kW.

Worked answer Link to this answer
Energy equals power multiplied by time. At 1,000 kW for 0.5 h the request is 500 kWh; at 500 kW it is 250 kWh.

Calculated results · kWh
ConfigurationIT demandResult (kWh)
Starting case1000 kW500
Challenge500 kW250

## Separate PUE from continuity | Datacenter Power Lesson 12

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/pue/

Lesson 12 / 12 · Facility energy planning

Separate PUE from continuity
How does assumed PUE change annual energy for the same 50 MW IT load?

By Mohammad Rezwan Khan · Engine 2.0.1 · Cite this lesson

Run this browser lesson →

Predict before you run
Write down your prediction, then change only the input below. In the interactive lesson, compare the starting case with the challenge and export a worksheet to retain your reasoning.

The two lesson configurations
InputStarting valueChallenge value
Assumed PUE1.25 ratio1.15 ratio

Reported quantity: kWh per 8,760 h. The live control accepts 1–2 ratio.

Worked answer Link to this answer
50,000 × 8,760 × 1.25 = 547,500,000 kWh; at 1.15 it is 503,700,000 kWh. The difference is 43,800,000 kWh at identical IT demand. PUE already includes non-IT overhead: do not add continuity losses to it again.

## DC-link EMT Study: Voltage Sag and Recovery | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/studies/emt/

Advanced study / EMT fundamentals

Inside a voltage sag
Explore a 200 ms DC-link transient. Change the circuit, replay the waveforms and check where the stored energy goes.

Original lesson by Mohammad Rezwan Khan · Circuit model dc-link-rlc-v1

Open the interactive EMT study →

The starting experiment
An ideal 800 V DC source feeds a 0.08 Ω resistor and 0.6 mH inductor, then a 12 mF capacitor in parallel with a 12.8 Ω load. At 40 ms the source drops to 400 V. At 120 ms it returns to 800 V.
The bus starts at 795.03 V, falls to 178.95 V and reaches a recovery peak of 1014.10 V. Stored energy delays the response and produces ringing in this underdamped circuit.

Generated from the same browser solver; shaded interval marks the source sag. The ideal source can absorb reverse current. Animation and chart samples are separate from integration steps.

Predict, run, explain
Predict whether the capacitor voltage changes instantly when the source falls.
Run the baseline, then double capacitance. Compare both the lowest voltage and recovery peak.
Lower series resistance. Explain how reduced damping changes the waveforms.
Halve the integration step and compare every plotted voltage sample. A small difference checks numerical convergence, not equipment fidelity.

The equations
Use amperes, volts, seconds, ohms, henries and farads internally:
L di/dt = Vsource − R i − Vbus
C dVbus/dt = i − Vbus/Rload
E = ½ L i² + ½ C Vbus²
ΔE = ∫ Vsource i dt − ∫ R i² dt − ∫ Vbus²/Rload dt

The initial DC state is i = 800/(0.08 + 12.8) A and Vbus = 12.8 i V. RK4 advances the electrical states and energy integrals together at 20 μs. Source events align with step boundaries. Output sampling is 100 μs; reported extrema use integration endpoints.

Computed baseline energy ledger over 200 ms
QuantityValue (J)
Net source energy8865.58248
Series resistor loss1867.21570
Resistive load energy6989.86041
Change in stored energy8.50636415
Numerical balance residual-1.37879852e-7

Reproduce the study
From a checkout containing this lesson:
python -m datacenter_twin.emt --preset voltage-sag --output outputs/emt.json
Download the ten input fields · Download all 2,001 samples and the energy ledger · Read the model and command guide.

What this circuit represents
A deliberately small electromagnetic-transient teaching circuit with an ideal DC-equivalent source, linear R-L-C elements and a constant-resistance load. It does not simulate converter switching, an AC grid, UPS controls, protection or a facility. Reverse source current and even negative capacitor voltage are allowed by the ideal equations; no diode or voltage clamp is modeled. Parameters are authored examples, with no PSCAD equivalence or measured calibration claim.
The twelve power-continuity lessons answer different questions about outage durations, capacity and finite battery energy.

Sources and validation
Reference Python solver and independent closed-form, energy and step-refinement tests.
PSCAD: introduction to time-domain electromagnetic transients (background; not validation of this model).
PSCAD: solution timestep versus channel plot step.
MathWorks: circuit differential equations and analytic solutions.

## Power Dynamics Studies: Converter Response and Grid Modes | Datacenter Twin Lab

URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/studies/power-dynamics/

Advanced power dynamics / five interactive studies

Follow a load change through the power system

Explore converter response, oscillation modes and interacting grid ports with the supplied Python study equations running in your browser.

Open the study studio →

Five configurable experimentsLocal Python + SciPyJSON and CSV exports

Choose a question, predict, then run
Study 1 / 5Load-step response
How quickly does PCC power follow a change from 0.5 to 0.6 pu?
Run an equilibrated 21-state converter chain. Compare the requested load, PCC response and DC-link voltage.

Study 2 / 5Modes and frequency response
What changes when the voltage-loop bandwidth changes?
Inspect eigenvalues, damping, dominant state participation and a sampled small-signal frequency response.

Study 3 / 5Synthetic load spectrum
Which part of a repeating load swing reaches the PCC?
Apply a bounded sinusoidal load and compare its time response and spectrum. The input is explicitly synthetic.

Study 4 / 5Phase model versus QSS
What does the reduced formulation leave out?
Compare the supplied 41-state abc and 21-state quasi-steady formulations, including their hand-set startup and a shared step at 0.04 s in a bounded 0.08 s window.

Study 5 / 5Interacting grid ports
Does a solved power flow imply stable dynamics?
Explore a modified nine-bus network with synchronous-machine, grid-forming, grid-following and data-center ports.

Read the system at two timescales

The twelve power-continuity lessons account for energy during outages. These advanced studies investigate the dynamics of idealized converter and grid models. For an introductory electromagnetic transient, begin with the separate DC-link RLC voltage-sag lesson.

What a mode tells you
For a linearized mode with eigenvalue λ = σ + jω, σ below zero indicates decay around that operating point. A positive σ indicates growth in the linearized model. Its frequency is |ω|/(2π) Hz; damping ratio is −σ/√(σ² + ω²). A converged power flow and stable dynamic modes answer different questions.

Run one controlled comparison
Select the load-step study and write a prediction before running.
Keep the starting settings, run, and inspect the recorded solver diagnostics.
Change only the DC capacitance from 2 to 3 pu. Run again and compare the transient shapes.
Export each applied result. Draft input edits are not part of an earlier result.

Runtime and reproducibility
The scientific runtime downloads only when you choose Run. Computation stays in a cancellable browser worker; there is no shared simulation backend or usage telemetry. The simpler course and DC-link study retain their lightweight JavaScript first calculation.
python -m pip install -r requirements-studies.lock
python -m datacenter_twin.research --study load-step --output outputs/load-step.json

Use a current checkout containing these studies. The historical v1.0.0 assets predate this addition. Results record the applied configuration, solver settings, assumptions, chart data and diagnostics. Per-unit values are normalized on the documented model bases, not automatically MW.

Provenance and interpretation
The owner supplied Python equivalents of MATLAB studies. The original MATLAB files and measured GPU trace were absent, so no MATLAB equivalence or measured-workload reproduction is claimed. The spectrum lesson uses a synthetic sinusoid. The phase-model comparison uses documented stiff integration instead of the original explicit Heun update. The nine-bus case is modified, not an unaltered standard benchmark. These are software teaching studies, not equipment or facility validation.

Sources
Study guide, equations provenance and adaptation map
Reviewed Python study implementation
Numerical regression and residual checks
SciPy integration methods and solver completion
Nine-bus test-network source and bibliography
